info.title: Cloud Independent Data Platform API
info.description:
## Cloud Independent Data Platform API

A unified API for managing **Apache Iceberg** data lakehouse infrastructure with
enterprise-grade **OIDC authentication** and **role-based access control**.

### Architecture

```
Client  →  API Gateway (this API)  →  Apache Polaris (Iceberg catalog)
                ↓                            ↓
           Keycloak (OIDC)            PostgreSQL (metadata)
                                             ↓
           Trino / Spark  ←──────── RustFS (S3 storage)
```

### Authentication

All endpoints (except `/api/platform/v1/health` and `/api/platform/v1/docs`) require a **Bearer token** from Keycloak.

```
Authorization: Bearer <your-keycloak-jwt-token>
```

Obtain a token via the BFF auth flow (`/api/platform/v1/auth/login`) or directly from Keycloak:

```bash
curl -X POST https://localhost/realms/example/protocol/openid-connect/token \
  -d "grant_type=password&client_id=polaris-frontend-client" \
  -d "username=<your-username>&password=<your-password>"
```

### Role-Based Access

| Role | Access Level |
|------|-------------|
| `service_admin` | Full platform management |
| `catalog_admin` | Catalog and role management |
| `data_writer` | Read + write data |
| `table_reader` | Read-only data access |

Lightweight session gate for reverse-proxy ``forward_auth``/``auth_request``.

Returns **204** when the request carries a valid authenticated BFF session
and **401** otherwise. Unlike ``/me`` (which always returns 200 with an
``authenticated`` flag so the SPA can tell "logged out" from "error"), this
endpoint signals authentication purely through the HTTP status code — which
is the only thing a proxy auth-subrequest inspects.

Used by the demo Caddy edge to gate the Langflow vhost (#354): an
unauthenticated browser hitting ``flow.<domain>`` gets a 401 here, which
Caddy turns into a redirect to the BFF login. No body, no token minting,
no audit log, no rate limit — safe to call on every gated page load.

Create an empty Iceberg table.

Admin-only for parity with namespace/warehouse create. The schema is
primitive-only (int / long / string / boolean / float / double / date /
timestamp / timestamptz); operators needing structs / maps / lists /
decimals should drive the catalog through dbt or a one-shot script.

Iceberg-REST API returns 409 when the table already exists. The shared
`_make_request` helper bubbles that up to the caller verbatim; we
translate to HTTPException so the same client error reaches the user

delete.description:
Delete a user from Keycloak. Requires admin role.

By default this removes only the Keycloak identity (backward
compatible). With ``?erase_data=true`` it first runs the GDPR
erasure cascade (CHM-PR-03): the subject's rows in the non-audit
personal-data stores are deleted and the audit stores are
pseudonymised (retained under a documented legal basis — see
``docs/compliance/data-inventory.md``). The cascade runs *before*
the identity delete so a failed cascade leaves the account intact
rather than orphaning data under a now-deleted user.

Get a table's active Iceberg partition spec (columns + transforms).

Exposes how the table is partitioned so a caller can introspect partition
fields without scanning data — a sibling to the ``/schema`` endpoint. Each
field's source column is resolved via the current schema. Dropped fields
(``void`` transform) are omitted; an unpartitioned table returns an empty

Views load from ``/views/{name}`` rather than ``/tables/{name}`` — loading

in the catalog browser. Returns the same ``{"columns": [...]}`` shape as
:func:`get_table_schema` so the frontend renders them identically.

Return the first ``limit`` rows of a table via Trino.

The query runs with the caller's JWT so Trino enforces
catalog/schema/table access per user. Read-only: the generic
statement validator in ``_preview_executor`` rejects anything
other than SELECT/SHOW/DESCRIBE/EXPLAIN/WITH/VALUES/USE/SET.

Return table-level lineage for an Iceberg/Trino view.

Runs ``SHOW CREATE VIEW`` via the caller's JWT, then parses the returned
view definition with sqlglot to extract upstream ``{catalog, namespace,
table}`` references. For non-views or missing objects we return a soft
empty response (HTTP 200) so callers can render "No lineage available"
without special-casing 4xx.

post.description: Execute SQL query. Supports 'type' field: 'trino' (default), 'spark', or 'flight'.

Run ``EXPLAIN`` or ``EXPLAIN ANALYZE`` on a Trino SQL statement.

Trino returns a single row with one column (``Query Plan``)
holding the formatted plan text.  We pass that through verbatim
plus a few stats so the UI can show the plan, the query id (for
cross-correlation with Jaeger / audit_log), and the wall-clock
duration.

Read-only: the inner statement is validated against the platform's
existing read-only guard so ``EXPLAIN INSERT …`` (which is
technically valid Trino but obviously a write surface) is
rejected.  Trino-only for now — Spark's ``df.explain()`` has a
different shape; can add later if customers ask.

than creating new jobs/runs/dataset versions every time.

1. the caller-supplied form field (typically the upstream pipeline's

  ``Content-Length`` (early exit) and while streaming the body

get.description:
Return a bipartite (dataset ⇄ job) graph rooted at ``root_id``.

When an ``X-Workspace`` header is present, the response is anchored to
the workspace's catalog set by default (only datasets with
``catalog ∈ workspace's catalogs`` are returned). Set
``cross_workspace=true`` to traverse boundaries: connected datasets
outside the anchor set are included and annotated with ``catalog``,
``owning_workspace`` (the slug of the workspace that OWNs the catalog,
or ``null`` if unowned), and ``external: true``. Cross-workspace nodes
expose metadata only; membership in the external workspace is NOT
required.

When no ``X-Workspace`` header is present the global/admin view is
returned unchanged (no catalog filter applied).

Trigram-similarity search across dataset and job names.

When an ``X-Workspace`` header is present, results are restricted by
default to the workspace's catalog set: datasets are filtered to
``catalog ∈ workspace's catalogs``, and jobs are filtered to those that
touch at least one in-workspace dataset (input or output). Set
``cross_workspace=true`` to widen the search back to the global index
(membership in the anchoring workspace is still required via the dep).
When no header is present the global/admin view is returned unchanged.

Audit M-15 / #262: the prior ``WHERE name ILIKE '%' || $1 || '%'``
clause forced a sequential scan because the ``pg_trgm`` GIN
operator class (``gin_trgm_ops`` on
``ix_datasets_name_trgm`` / ``ix_jobs_name_trgm``) only indexes
the trigram operators (``%``, ``<%``, ``%>``) — ILIKE is not
among them, so the GIN index sat unused and Postgres scanned
every row at search time. The fix switches the predicate to the
trigram similarity operator ``%``, which lets the planner use
the index. ``similarity(...)`` in the SELECT list (kept for the
score) shares the same ``pg_trgm.similarity_threshold`` GUC as
the operator, so the SELECT score lines up with the filter
threshold. EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the SQE Postgres with 5k datasets
confirms a ``Bitmap Index Scan on ix_datasets_name_trgm`` when
``enable_seqscan = off`` — the planner picks it naturally once
tables grow past the "seq-scan is cheaper" threshold
(~10k rows in practice).

Dataset detail with current schema, facets, and per-source attribution.

Beyond the original ``{id, name, namespace, schema}`` shape, the
response now carries:

- ``facets``: every facet ever recorded for the dataset's
  ``current_version_id``, grouped by ``facet_name``. Each group has
  one ``authoritative`` row (the current trust-resolution winner)
  and a ``superseded`` list of every other contributor for that
  name, ordered by trust score DESC then ingestion recency.
- ``attribution``: per-source rollup of facet counts and ingestion
  timestamps for the dataset's current version, ranked by most
  recent contribution.

A dataset with no ``current_version_id`` (placeholder, e.g. a
downstream alias created before its producing run completed) gets
empty ``facets`` and ``attribution`` lists rather than a 4xx — the
schema panel is still useful and the front-end is expected to
handle the empty case.

Workspace scoping: when an ``X-Workspace`` header is present, the
dataset's ``catalog`` must be in the workspace's catalog set or the
endpoint returns 404 — full detail (including all stored facet
``content`` JSONB) is never served for a cross-workspace dataset. When
no header is present the global/admin view is returned unchanged.

the physical column ("crm.customers.email_address").

The endpoint is intentionally read-only and tolerant — a dataset
with no matching mapping returns an empty ``matches`` list and the
parsed ``resolved_*`` so the UI can show a "no ontology mapping
yet" hint without a 4xx.

visible only if it touches at least one in-workspace dataset (an input
or output whose ``catalog`` is in the workspace's catalog set); otherwise

with no run history). The old default; renamed to be self-describing.

are excluded — their lineage is intact via the canonical, so they are
not genuine orphans.

indicate a resolver bug (the read-side walk only follows one hop).

Wire shape for ``GET /api/platform/v1/lineage/datasets/{id}``.

Extends the original ``{id, name, namespace, schema}`` shape with
facets (grouped by ``facet_name``) and per-source attribution. When
the dataset has no ``current_version_id`` yet — for example a
placeholder created by a downstream emitter before the producing
run completed — both ``facets`` and ``attribution`` are empty.

``schema`` collides with ``BaseModel.schema()`` — we expose the
wire field as ``schema`` via a serialization alias on a renamed
attribute, and silence the protected-namespace warning since this
is an external API contract, not an internal model attribute.

DatasetOntologyResponse.title: DatasetOntologyResponse
DatasetOntologyResponse.description:
Wire shape for the cross-module ontology lookup.

``resolved`` carries the parsed (catalog, schema, table) the lookup
used so a UI can debug why a match did or didn't appear.

DigestSummary.title: DigestSummary
DigestSummary.description: Structured contents of one digest.  Persisted as JSONB.

DuplicateDatasetEntry.description: One dataset within a duplicates group (parser-identity match).

DuplicatesResponse.title: DuplicatesResponse
DuplicatesResponse.description:
Wire shape for ``GET .../admin/duplicates``.

The response carries exactly one of ``duplicates``, ``orphans``, or

fields are ``None`` so the OpenAPI doc is honest about which keys to

EntityContext.title: EntityContext
EntityContext.description: One entity in the current draft, as the prompt input.

EventLogEntry.title: EventLogEntry
EventLogEntry.description: A single durable domain event from the ``event_log`` table.

EventLogResponse.title: EventLogResponse
EventLogResponse.description:

FacetGroup.title: FacetGroup
FacetGroup.description:
Facets for one ``facet_name``, split by authority.

``authoritative`` is the single row currently flagged
``is_authoritative=TRUE`` for that facet name on the dataset's
current dataset_version. May be ``None`` if every row for that name
was superseded by writes on a different dataset_version — a defensive
case the read path tolerates.

FacetValue.title: FacetValue
FacetValue.description:
One ``lineage.facets`` row, scoped to a single source's contribution.

Surfaces the source name (joined from ``lineage.sources``), trust
score, raw content payload, and ingestion timestamp so the UI can
render the authoritative-vs-superseded split for the side panel.

FeatureAccessRuleBody.title: FeatureAccessRuleBody
FeatureAccessRuleBody.description: An allow/deny rule for one principal on a feature.

ForwarderFilterInfo.title: ForwarderFilterInfo
ForwarderFilterInfo.description:
Snapshot of the configured filters.

``None`` means "no filter — forward every value".  An empty list
would be confusable so we keep it as ``None`` end-to-end and let
the UI decide how to render it.

ForwarderHealthResponse.title: ForwarderHealthResponse
ForwarderHealthResponse.description:
Operational view of the OCSF event forwarder.

All values are read straight off the in-memory manager / config.
No DB calls — this endpoint is safe to poll at any cadence.

GrantCreate.title: GrantCreate
GrantCreate.description: Request model for creating a grant.

privilege.title: Privilege
privilege.description: Normal mode: USE, SELECT, MODIFY, CREATE, DROP, MANAGE, ALL

access_types.title: Access Types
access_types.description: Advanced mode: exact polaris service-def access types (e.g. ['namespace-list']). Mutually exclusive with privilege.

level.title: Level
level.description: Advanced mode resource level: catalog | namespace | table. Defaults to the deepest level implied by the namespace/table given.

grant_option.title: Grant Option
grant_option.description: SQL WITH GRANT OPTION: let the grantee re-grant (and revoke) this privilege on this resource. Maps to Ranger's delegateAdmin. Off by default — holding a privilege never implies being able to grant it.

GrantRequest.title: GrantRequest
GrantRequest.description:
Normal mode (``privilege``) or advanced mode (``access_types`` + ``level``).

Normal mode expands a grouped privilege into one policy per resource level, with each
seed expanded through Ranger's ``impliedGrants``. Advanced mode writes exactly the
access types given, at exactly the level given, for callers who know the Ranger
service definition and want no expansion applied on their behalf.

GraphEdge.title: GraphEdge
GraphEdge.description:
A directed dataset⇄job edge with run-level evidence counts.

``contributing_sources`` is a flat list of source *names* retained
for backwards compatibility — the frontend already consumes it to
fan out per-source parallel edges.

``source_attribution`` was added per audit I-23 (#254) so edges
carry the same ``{source_id, source_name}`` shape as nodes (see
the lineage-core spec's "Source-attribution in graph response"
requirement). It is additive — every entry corresponds to a name
in ``contributing_sources`` and clients that only read the names
keep working.

GraphNode.title: GraphNode
GraphNode.description:
A dataset or job node in the bipartite lineage graph.

``id`` is the prefixed string form (``dataset:<uuid>`` / ``job:<uuid>``);
``last_run`` carries a small dict shape ``{"id", "state", "ended_at"}``
for jobs, and is ``None`` for datasets.

Workspace-scope fields (present when a workspace context is active):
- ``catalog``: the catalog the dataset belongs to (populated from the
  denormalized ``lineage.datasets.catalog`` column).
- ``external``: ``True`` when the dataset is outside the anchoring
  workspace's catalog set (only populated when ``cross_workspace=True``).
- ``owning_workspace``: slug of the workspace that OWNs the catalog,
  or ``None`` when no workspace claims ownership.

GraphResponse.title: GraphResponse
GraphResponse.description:
Bipartite graph payload returned by the graph endpoint.

``truncated`` flips true when the walk hit the node cap; the caller
can re-request with a lower depth or a tighter root scope.

``column_edges`` is populated from ``columnLineageDatasetFacet`` rows
on the visible datasets (MR3). Defaults to an empty list when no
column-lineage facets exist; old clients that ignore the field stay
on the wire contract.

ImportFormat.title: ImportFormat
ImportFormat.description: Wire enum the router accepts; aligns with ``rdflib.Graph.parse``.

namespaces.title: Namespaces
namespaces.description: ``{prefix, uri}`` pairs harvested from the source graph.

warnings.title: Warnings
warnings.description: Human-readable notes about skipped / fuzzy mappings.

ImportPreview.title: ImportPreview
ImportPreview.description:
Shape the router returns from ``/import/preview``.

The frontend renders ``entities`` + ``relations`` as checklists,
surfaces ``warnings`` in a banner, and includes ``namespaces`` in a
"we'll create these prefixes" hint.

JobDetailResponse.title: JobDetailResponse
JobDetailResponse.description:
Wire shape for ``GET /api/platform/v1/lineage/jobs/{id}``.

``id`` is the prefixed form (``job:<uuid>``); ``runs[].id`` keeps the
bare UUID because run ids are not graph-node identifiers.

JobRunSummary.title: JobRunSummary
JobRunSummary.description:
One run row in a job-detail response.

``id`` is the bare run UUID (run identifiers do not carry a kind
prefix; only dataset/job node identifiers do).

``sql_text`` / ``sql_dialect`` carry the OL 2.0 SQLJobFacet contents
captured at ingest time and persisted on the run's ``job_version``.
Both are nullable: producers that don't emit the facet (or
pre-migration-026 rows) surface as ``None``, and the frontend
renders an "SQL not captured" placeholder in that case.

LogoutResponse.title: LogoutResponse
LogoutResponse.description: Body of /logout — the OIDC end-session URL for the browser to follow.

context_truncated.title: Context Truncated
context_truncated.description: True when the prompt was trimmed to fit per-section or token caps. When set, ``context_truncation_reason`` carries the human-readable hint.

context_truncation_reason.title: Context Truncation Reason
context_truncation_reason.description: Why the context was truncated, e.g. 'truncated to first 30 tables (of 142)'.

MergeRequest.title: MergeRequest
MergeRequest.description:
Validated request body for ``POST .../datasets/merge``.

Static checks (every field parses, no self-merge, no internal dupes,
duplicate list non-empty) run via Pydantic so they reject before
the SQL layer (audit I-7 / #238). Existence + alias-as-canonical
checks remain in the handler — they need a DB roundtrip — and also
return 422 with a specific detail.

MetadataCatalogListResponse.description: Response model for metadata catalog listing.

MetadataNamespaceListResponse.title: MetadataNamespaceListResponse
MetadataNamespaceListResponse.description: Response model for metadata namespace listing.

MetadataPartitionSpecResponse.title: MetadataPartitionSpecResponse
MetadataPartitionSpecResponse.description:
Response model for a table's active Iceberg partition spec.

``fields`` describes how the table is partitioned — one entry per active
partition field, each with its partition-column ``name``, the ``transform``
applied (``identity``/``day``/``hour``/``bucket[N]``/``truncate[N]``/…), and
the ``source_column`` it derives from (resolved via the current schema;
``None`` if the source id can't be resolved). Dropped fields (``void``
transform) are omitted. An unpartitioned table returns an empty ``fields``.

MetadataTableListResponse.title: MetadataTableListResponse
MetadataTableListResponse.description: Response model for metadata table listing.

MetadataViewListResponse.title: MetadataViewListResponse
MetadataViewListResponse.description:
Response model for metadata view listing.

Shape mirrors :class:`MetadataTableListResponse` — each entry is an Iceberg
REST view identifier ``{"namespace": [...], "name": "..."}`` — so the
frontend can treat views and tables uniformly when building the catalog
tree.

NamespaceUpdate.title: NamespaceUpdate
NamespaceUpdate.description: Request model for updating namespace properties.

NodeAttribution.title: NodeAttribution
NodeAttribution.description: One ``lineage.sources`` row that contributed evidence for a node.

so the lineage detail panel can show business names ("Customer.email")
alongside the physical column ("crm.customers.email_address").

apply.description: false = dry-run plan; true = execute the downscope

RescopeServicePrincipalBody.title: RescopeServicePrincipalBody
RescopeServicePrincipalBody.description:
Downscope an existing bootstrap-seeded engine principal (slice-2 migration).

``apply`` defaults to false — a dry-run plan that flips nothing. Only the
allowlisted engine principals (Trino/Spark) may be targeted; the service
refuses any other name.

RevokeRequest.title: RevokeRequest
RevokeRequest.description: Mirror of :class:`GrantRequest` — normal or advanced mode.

SPAuthorizer.title: SPAuthorizer
SPAuthorizer.description: Which least-privilege backend authorizes the principal (Decision C).

SPCredentialMode.title: SPCredentialMode
SPCredentialMode.description:
How storage credentials reach the engine (Decision B).

``VENDED`` (the safe default) — Polaris vends short-lived, scoped storage
credentials; ``table-data-read`` is the real gate so a TVF static-key
bypass cannot bite. ``STATIC`` — the engine holds a static object-store
key; the feature MUST keep the TVF gate fail-closed (never add the identity
to ``object_store_admin_roles`` / broad prefixes) and flags it less-safe.

SPMode.title: SPMode
SPMode.description: Whether the service principal may write or only read.

SagaStepResult.title: SagaStepResult
SagaStepResult.description: Result of a single saga step.

SampleEventBody.description: Sample event for ws-admin render/test: the would-be HTTP body or S3 fields.

ScheduleResponse.title: ScheduleResponse
ScheduleResponse.description: API shape — flattens dataclass + serialises ISO datetimes.

SchedulerHealthResponse.title: SchedulerHealthResponse
SchedulerHealthResponse.description:
Public liveness probe for the scheduler loop.

Returned by ``GET /schedules/health`` — an unauthenticated
endpoint (k8s liveness, alertmanager) so the body must contain
**no sensitive detail**:

- No ``last_error`` string (#212): may include internal hostnames,
  DB-connection strings, exception traces. ``had_recent_error``
  and ``last_error_at`` give callers enough signal to correlate
  against their own logs.
- No ``runners`` list (#212): runner-type names leak deployment
  topology. ``runner_count`` is a coarse health indicator.
- No ``token_exchange_enabled`` (#212): config flag that aids
  phishing planning when public.

Operators wanting the full detail use the admin-gated
``/api/platform/v1/admin/scheduler/health`` (separate router) or
the structured log stream.

SearchHit.title: SearchHit
SearchHit.description:
One row in a ``/search`` response.

``id`` is the prefixed form (``dataset:<uuid>`` / ``job:<uuid>``) per
the wire-shape convention documented in
``data_platform.lineage.routers.query`` (audit C-5 / #228, I-9 / #240).

Severity.title: Severity
Severity.description: Mapped 1:1 to the priorities used in ``docs/SIEM_DETECTION_RULES.md``.

SourceAttribution.title: SourceAttribution
SourceAttribution.description:
Per-source attribution row for a dataset's current_version_id.

Counts facets contributed and tracks first/last ingestion so the
side panel can rank sources by recency and explain why a particular
fact about the dataset is shown.

SparkConnectSession.description: A persisted per-principal Spark Connect session (metadata only).

SparkSessionRequest.description: A user may select only a reviewed, server-defined resource shape.

storage_location.description: Custom S3 location for table data (overrides catalog default)

create_bucket.title: Create Bucket
create_bucket.description: Create the S3 bucket from storage_location if it doesn't exist

endpoint_internal.description: Internal S3 endpoint used by the Polaris server itself for metadata writes

path_style_access.title: Path Style Access
path_style_access.description: True for MinIO/rustfs and other path-style S3 implementations

allowed_locations.description: Locations Polaris is allowed to write under. Default if unset: bucket root of ``default_base_location`` — overlaps when multiple warehouses share a bucket, so prefer scoped paths like ``s3://bucket/warehouse-a/``

drop_with_purge_enabled.title: Drop With Purge Enabled
drop_with_purge_enabled.description: Allow Trino/dbt to DROP TABLE with data purge

StorageConfig.title: StorageConfig
StorageConfig.description:
Per-warehouse S3 storage configuration.

All fields are optional. Anything left ``None`` falls back to the env
defaults below; callers wanting a unique bucket / prefix supply at
least ``default_base_location`` (and usually ``allowed_locations``)
so their warehouse doesn't overlap with others sharing the bucket.

The wire field names on this model are pythonic; we translate them
into Polaris's kebab-case keys before forwarding to the client.

SubmitRunRequest.title: SubmitRunRequest
SubmitRunRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /runs/submit`` — an ephemeral one-shot run.

The Databricks ``SubmitRun`` analogue: run a job *once*, immediately,
without persisting a cron schedule. There is no ``cron_expression`` /
``timezone`` (nothing is scheduled) and no ``enabled`` flag. The run
executes under the *caller's* own identity, so there's no separate
owner to authorize.

``notify_targets`` reuses the same SSRF allowlist as schedules (an
authenticated user must not be able to turn a one-shot run into an
SSRF gadget any more than a scheduled one).

SyncIssue.title: SyncIssue
SyncIssue.description: A detected sync issue between systems.

TableColumn.title: TableColumn
TableColumn.description:
One column in a CREATE TABLE request.

`type` maps directly to an Iceberg primitive type name: int, long,
string, boolean, float, double, date, timestamp, timestamptz. The
Iceberg-REST spec accepts more complex types (struct/map/list,
decimal(p,s), fixed(n)) — those are intentionally out of scope here.
Operators wanting non-primitive columns should drive the catalog
through dbt or a one-shot script for now.

TeachRequest.title: TeachRequest
TeachRequest.description:
Request body for the teach endpoint.

Carries both the Correction fields and the optimistic-lock fields that the
knowledge-edit apply path requires. Lock fields default to None — the apply
path falls back to the current lock/hash when they are omitted, matching
the behaviour of POST /knowledge-edits/apply.

``version_id`` is required (diverges from brief's field list) because
KnowledgeEditService.apply needs to know which draft to edit and there is
no unique-draft constraint that would let the server infer it.

resolved_sql.title: Resolved Sql
resolved_sql.description: Pre-resolved SQL to execute instead of reading from file_path.

TopActor.title: TopActor
TopActor.description: Aggregate row for the "top N most active users" section.

TriggerRunRequest.title: TriggerRunRequest
TriggerRunRequest.description: Request to trigger a quality run.

TrustProfileBody.title: TrustProfileBody
TrustProfileBody.description:
Validated request body for ``PUT .../sources/{id}/trust``.

A trust profile is a flat ``{facet_name: int_score}`` map: keys are
OpenLineage facet names (or the literal ``other`` fallback key), values
are non-negative integers on the 0–200 scale (see
``bootstrap/trust_defaults.py``). Anything else — nested objects, string
scores, stray fields like ``producer_regex`` — gets a 422 from FastAPI's
Pydantic validation, so a steward following stale docs cannot silently
overwrite ``trust_profile`` with garbage that the trust resolver would
then treat as ``{}`` (and fall back to 50 for every facet).

UpdateScheduleRequest.title: UpdateScheduleRequest
UpdateScheduleRequest.description:
All fields optional — partial update.

The keyword ``default=None`` form (rather than positional
``Field(None, …)``) keeps Pyright happy: Pyright doesn't always
recognise Pydantic's positional-default argument as making the
field optional, leading to spurious "missing argument" warnings
on call sites that pass only a subset of fields.

UpstreamTable.title: UpstreamTable
UpstreamTable.description: A single upstream table reference extracted from a view definition.

ViewLineageResponse.title: ViewLineageResponse
ViewLineageResponse.description:

``is_view`` is ``False`` when the target is not a view (plain table, or the
object doesn't exist). In that case ``upstream_tables`` is empty and
``sql`` is ``None``; the frontend renders "No lineage available".

column_lineage_hints.title: Column Lineage Hints
column_lineage_hints.description: Observed column-level lineage edges between the tables in ``tables``. The proposer surfaces these as join hints in the LLM prompt so the model proposes relations grounded in actual data flow instead of guessing from column names (#319).
